concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.note: Central concept: the entire torah discusses the state of consciousness required during prayer. No bechina edges exist in the dataset for this torah.

The torah describes two levels of bittul during prayer: (1) not being aware of other people, (2) not being aware of oneself at all — only Hashem. The second level is drawn from Torah #55 (Abba Shaul).
The metaphor used: during prayer one stands in the King's palace, so one's yeshut (selfhood) is nullified — there is only the King Himself.
The negative quality that must be nullified during prayer. 'יֵשׁוּתוֹ נִתְבַּטֵּל' — his selfhood is annulled.
